speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) for the past five years, what is the number of complaints received pertaining to the noise and smell generated from live chickens located in HDB estates and private residential estates respectively; and (b) whether there will be a review of chicken rearing policy in HDB flats, private residential apartments and private landed residential properties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: When HDB gets complaints about chicken rearing in HDB flats, we work closely with agencies to engage the flat owners to make alternative arrangements to rehome their chickens where necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Private residential owners who keep chickens on their property are also urged to do their part to minimise any inconveniences to their neighbours, such as noise and smell.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Under the Community Dispute Management Framework, disputing parties can seek mediation at the Community Mediation Centre or, in more intractable cases, refer the matter to the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks will continue to work with our partners to raise public awareness on responsible pet ownership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks and HDB review pet ownership policies regularly to safeguard public health, while balancing the needs of different segments of the community.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: I hope that the ban on chicken or live chicken imports from Malaysia have not prompted more Singaporeans to rear more chickens in their homes, especially private homes.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: But during my home visits to a private estate in Nanyang, I definitely experienced an increase in the number of complaints.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: The Senior Minister of State said that there were 2,100 complaints about chickens in private estates, compared to 1,700 in HDB estates.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Which means that – okay, so we have more.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: I understand that, currently, we allow private estate home owners to have up to 10 chickens in the household.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: I wonder whether the Government is prepared to review the number so as to reduce the number of complaints about chickens.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: My second supplementary question is, how many of the complaints have ended up being resolved and how many complaints have ended up going to the mediation centre, as explained by the Senior Minister of State?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Whether we will see more chickens, I do not know.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Personally, I have not come across many of such cases.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: NParks, HDB and MND do not track the number of chickens we have in residential properties in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: As for the Member's question on whether most of these issues have been resolved, I think many of them are between neighbours, especially when you are talking about the feedback around chickens in private residential estates.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We do not track how many have gone to the Community Mediation Centre and how many have been resolved through that process, but we understand that many of the complaints are between neighbours and, together with the local advisors, they come together and talk through the issues as a community.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I will take Mr Louis Ng and then Assoc Prof Jamus Lim.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I just ask, on a serious note, specifically, under what legislation do we ban the keeping of chickens in HDB flats?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Because I do believe we have been challenged before and maybe it is under the Memorandum of Lease that the people who buy HDB flats signed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But could I just ask, specifically, which legislation prevents this?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: One is the role of NParks, which looks at this from the point of view of public health concerns.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We know there are diseases that can jump from animal hosts to humans – zoonotic diseases – and this is something we pay a lot of attention to.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The other concern, from NParks' point of view, is really about the welfare of the animals – whether there are abuses or cruelty to animals.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Those are the things that NParks looks after.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Flat owners are not allowed to keep any animal and not allowed to keep chickens under the Memorandum of Lease in the flat, or any part of the common area of the building, unless approved by HDB.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And to add on to the point that Mr Ng is also alluding to, instances of HDB residents keeping chickens in the flats are actually rare.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: If there are such cases, please let us know, we will work with the agencies to advise the owners to make alternative arrangements to home the chickens.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: The last supplementary question on this, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, please.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The first is to obtain the assurance from the Senior Minister of State that the standard operating procedure is that the first resort is for mediation, rather than slapping the violators with any kind of fine.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And I mention this because, I recall, as a child, going through experiments where you would hatch chickens from eggs and you would keep them in the flat while they grew.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: We do not want to penalise young children and students who are conducting little experiments in this fashion.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The second question has to do with whether the Ministry has thought about what happens when there are community chickens and in particular, roosters.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And I mention this because, in Sengkang, we had incidences of reports of community roosters and, as you can imagine, no one necessarily lays claim to these roosters.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Does NParks then intervene to assist the Town Council in managing early rooster crowing?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: A last word on the matter, Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Yes, I am surprised there is a fair bit of interest around chickens today.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And secondly, whether the animal is treated well or if there is abuse or cruelty – the issue of animal welfare.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On Assoc Prof Lim's second supplementary question around the community rooster, perhaps I could seek a clarification from Assoc Prof Lim, just to understand a bit more about where he is coming from and the specific case he cited in Sengkang, because I am not familiar with it.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Is it something the Member is supportive of – to have the community rooster, but for it to be better taken care of, or is he asking NParks to come and do something about the rooster?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Just to clarify, in the end, as you can imagine, in the community situation, there are those that are pro-rooster and anti-rooster.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: As it turns out, in the end, the rooster was removed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: But I am wondering whether NParks has standard advice for this kind of situations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I believe it was by the Town Council, in collaboration with NParks.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I think he reflects the tensions that we all face as advisors and as Members of Parliament on the ground.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Different segments of the community, different segments of our residents, have different desires and preferences.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And, oftentimes, as Government agencies, we do want to work with the local advisors and, in this case, the Town Council, to see how we can amicably resolve it.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Removing the rooster may be one option but there are many other ways of finding ways of accommodating.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: There are many ways to tackle the issue.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Ultimately, the assurance that we give to members of the public and our residents is that we want to work together with them, different segments of the community.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: At the end of the day, it is about our home, our neighbourhood, and we want to see how we can work together.
